items.note: The page sets up Theta, checks well-definedness and the wrap sign, extends linewise via iota D_+, and reaches M_C(f,g)=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=f*g/T with the contraction, following the paper's section 'Complex convolution by a coefficient twist' (lines 4298-4347) and spelling out the 'why' the assignment asked for.
'Let zeta=e^{pi i/r}, so zeta^r=-1. Define Theta: C[x_d]/(x_d^r-1) -> R_r by x_d -> zeta y', with R_r=C[y]/(y^r+1) introduced earlier, exactly as in the paper.

Well-definedness from (zeta y)^r=(-1)(-1)=1 using zeta^r=-1 and y^r=-1; diagonality from 'Theta(x_d^k)=zeta^k y^k'; isomorphism with inverse zeta^{-k}; sup-norm preservation justified by |zeta^{+-k}|=1. Matches paper lines 4308-4312.

Writes k+l=j+hr with h in {0,1}, gives the factor zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j(zeta^r)^h(-1)^h=zeta^j, concludes the y^j coefficient is zeta^j times the cyclic coefficient so untwisting by zeta^{-j} recovers it; a correct r=2 worked example (constant term f0g0+f1g1, y-coefficient i(f0g1+f1g0)) is added.

Defines iota (M=T/r lines read as polynomials), D_+-, notes iota D_+ is linewise Theta with inverse D_- iota^{-1}, that M_r convolves the first d-1 axes over R_r and already divides by T, while * convolves all d axes; the identity is reached at the paper's own level ('Consequently'), and the contraction is shown explicitly via ||M_C(f,g)|| <= ||iota D_+ f|| ||iota D_+ g|| = ||f|| ||g|| using the rM-average argument for M_r (paper lines 3378-3387).
